How a recovery works

Method, as implemented in failure_recovery.py + the controller's transition machinery

A path switch is a make-before-break transaction, not a single flow-mod swap. The controller prepares the new path, activates it, commits once both ingress changes are acknowledged, drains the old path while its rules are retained, and only then cleans the old rules up. Each stage writes a row to transitions.csv with its status; a transaction on this page is those rows grouped back together, and its duration is the recorded gap between the transaction's start and completion rows — measured, never estimated.

Link failures enter through OpenFlow port-status events: a down port is mapped to its link, the outage is logged, and when the failed link is on the active path the controller reroutes to the surviving path. The failure tracker attaches the first reroute after the failure to the outage and measures recovery from the samples that follow it — utilization back under the recovery threshold — so time-to-reroute and time-to-recover are computed from the events themselves.

An honest gap is shown as a gap: if no run has recorded a link_down event or a failures.csv row yet, this page says so instead of filling the section with a congestion reroute relabelled as a failure.
